scope: STATE AND CITY POLICE — spending, strength, outcomes. Three levels of resolution: Union money resolves to the line item (sibling files); state money resolves to the Police major head per state (RBI State Finances 2025-26 Appendix II 'iii) Police', ₹ lakh, 2023-24 Accounts → 2025-26 BE for all 28 states, J&K and Puducherry; Uttar Pradesh's own Grant 26 MH 2055 / 4055 / 109 series 2008-09 → 2026-27; PRS 'district police' lines for the other four largest forces as reported:), with strength and per-capita figures reported: while BPR&D is down (DoPO Jan 2020 via a Rajya Sabha answer, Jan 2023 and Jan 2024 via PRS transcriptions, Jan 2022 IJR indicators folded into the notes; women's strength Jan 2023 via a Lok Sabha answer; absolute counts derived from the per-lakh ratios and flagged); city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (17 commissionerates listed on the UP and Maharashtra police sites) and the void. Outcomes are rates: NHRC deaths in police custody FY2021-22 → FY2025-26 by state (LS UQ 5115), NCRB Crime in India 2024 chapter 16A/16B by state, each over actual police strength and population, with the state government's party as text. Symmetry: BJP-run beside opposition-run states on per-capita spend, per-lakh strength, vacancy share and custodial-death rate. Leaves out: Union police demands, CAPFs, prisons, forensic and fire services, procurement, pay scales, cases — in sibling files.

claims.lab: Uttar Pradesh: police spend per capita, share of state spending, strength and NHRC police-custody death cases, FY2023-24 → FY2024-25
claims.d: Revenue spend on Police 2023-24 Accounts ₹25,314.81 crore ÷ population 2022 2340.94 lakh = ₹1,081 per person; 5.89% of the state's revenue expenditure (all-states 4.67%). Strength 01.01.2024: sanctioned 181, actual 134 per lakh (vacancy share 26.0%, derived; all-India 197/155, 21.3%). NHRC cases registered in respect of deaths in police custody, FY2024-25 (registration year): 11 = 3.51 per lakh actual police (≈313,686, derived: Jan 2024 per-lakh ratio × 2022 projected population) and 0.47 per crore population; NCRB CII 2024: 0 (Tables 16A.1 not-on-remand + 16A.2 on-remand; as provided by the state). Population vintages differ: the FY2023-24 spend and the 01.01.2024 per-lakh ratio are both put over the NCRB 2022 projection, which inflates per-capita spend by about 2–3% and the derived police count by a similar margin; DoPO's own population base is unknown (see killIf). Government in the period: BJP (Yogi Adityanath, CM since 2017-03-19) (party as text; not a filter).

claims.innocentReading: Per-capita spend tracks state fiscal capacity, urbanisation, insurgency grants and pay-commission timing more than policing policy; vacancy shares reflect recruitment cycles and court stays; custodial-death counts are small numbers (0–30) whose year-to-year swings are mostly noise, and NHRC counts intimations (including hospital deaths of detainees) that NCRB's state-supplied tables may not.
claims.upgradeIf: BPR&D DoPO 2024/2025 tables reachable (absolute strengths, expenditure by state) and the state's own demand for grants fetched.
claims.killIf: RBI revises the 2023-24 Accounts figure, or DoPO's population base differs materially from the NCRB 2022 projection used here.

claims.lab: Symmetry: BJP-run beside opposition-run states — party in FY2024-25; spend 2023-24 Accounts, strength 01.01.2024, NHRC police-custody death cases FY2024-25 (medians)
claims.d: Party assignment is the CM's party in FY2024-25 (fetched lists); the spend and strength readings predate it. BJP-run (UP, GJ, MP, RJ, CT, HR, UT, AS, AR, GA, TR): median police spend per capita 2023-24 ₹1,727; median actual police per lakh (Jan 2024) 174; median vacancy share 20.7% (derived, 1 − actual/sanctioned); median NHRC custodial-death cases FY2024-25 per lakh actual police 6.3. The ₹1,727 and 20.7% medians are Chhattisgarh's values, produced in 2023-24 under the outgoing INC government (BJP from 2023-12-13); Rajasthan likewise was INC for ~8.5 months of 2023-24 — regrouped by the party in power in 2023-24 the BJP per-capita median would be about ₹1,937 and the opposition median unchanged. Opposition-run (KA, KL, TN, WB, TG, PB, HP, JH): median per capita ₹1,458; median actual per lakh 156.5; median vacancy share 15.5%; median custodial-death rate 7.56 (7.555 rounded) per lakh police. Large states (population ≥ 3 crore, NCRB 2022 projection; this drops CT 299.5 lakh and HR 299.7 lakh and adds AS and JH): BJP-run UP/GJ/MP/RJ/AS per capita ₹[1081, 997, 912, 1049, 1478], actual per lakh [134, 132, 123, 119, 167], vacancy [26.0, 23.3, 14.6, 16.8, 13.9]%, NHRC cases FY2024-25 [11, 14, 8, 9, 13] = [3.51, 14.95, 7.57, 9.40, 21.93] per lakh police; opposition-run KA/KL/TN/WB/TG/PB/JH per capita ₹[1258, 1212, 1343, 1012, 2356, 2615, 1573], actual per lakh [141, 153, 160, 106, 161, 233, 152], vacancy [15.1, 11.0, 7.0, 36.5, 28.4, 15.9, 27.3]%, NHRC cases [2, 5, 5, 7, 1, 6, 7] = [2.10, 9.16, 4.07, 6.69, 1.64, 8.42, 11.77] per lakh police. Reading: the BJP-run median is pulled up by small north-eastern states (AR, TR, GA) on per-capita spend and per-lakh strength; among large states the two groups overlap on every measure (custodial-death rates 3.51–21.93 vs 1.64–11.77). Excluded from both groups: Bihar (JD(U)-led NDA), Odisha and Andhra Pradesh (government changed mid-2024), Maharashtra (coalition) — shown separately in baseRates — and Manipur (BJP CM to 2025-02-09, then President's Rule from 2025-02-13; no 2023-24 per-capita row in this file). The edge anchors the file's symmetry check on BPR&D (strength source) and MHA (NHRC answer source); it does not assert a BPR&D-to-MHA relation.

claims.lab: Two official counts of deaths in police custody: NCRB (calendar 2024) 65 vs NHRC cases registered (FY2024-25) 140 — NHRC is 2.15× NCRB
claims.d: NCRB Crime in India 2024 Vol III Tables 16A.1–16A.2 (data 'as provided by States/UTs'; the chapter carries the caveat 'States/UTs may not be compared purely on the basis of crime figures'): 65 deaths in police custody/lockup in 2024 all-India (states 63: Gujarat 17, Maharashtra 16, Rajasthan 8, MP 6; UP 0, WB 0, Bihar 1, Assam 1). NHRC cases registered in respect of death in police custody (LS UQ 5115): 140 in FY2024-25 (Gujarat 14, Maharashtra 14, Assam 13, UP 11, Bihar 10); FY2023-24 157 gives the same 2.4× result, which neutralises the calendar-vs-fiscal mismatch. Largest single-state gaps: Assam NCRB 1 vs NHRC 13 (BJP-run), UP 0 vs 11 (BJP-run), Bihar 1 vs 10 (JD(U)-led NDA), West Bengal 0 vs 7 (AITC) — the gap is not a party pattern. Gujarat and Maharashtra run the other way (NCRB higher: 17 vs 14, 16 vs 14). Base rate: NHRC exceeds NCRB in 18 of the 27 states with both figures; 7 of 28 states return NCRB 0 against NHRC > 0 (AP, JH, ML, OD, UP, UK, WB); 13 of 28 states return NCRB 0.

claims.innocentReading: Different definitions and periods: NHRC registers every intimation of a death of a person in police custody within 24 hours, including deaths in hospital after arrest, and counts by registration date rather than date of death; NCRB counts calendar-year deaths as returned by state crime records bureaux (its Table 16A.2 already includes persons in police/judicial remand — 25 of the 65 are remand deaths — so remand is not the distinguishing feature); the gap says the two series are not interchangeable, not that one is falsified.
claims.upgradeIf: NHRC's own annual report tables and NCRB's definitional note are fetched and the two series reconciled state by state.
claims.killIf: NCRB's 2024 table is revised, or NHRC's FY figures are shown to include judicial-custody intimations (checked: LS UQ 5115's annexure is headed 'death in Police custody', so judicial-custody intimations are excluded; the clause stays as a standing check).

claims.lab: J&K's police line in the RBI table falls 73% between 2023-24 Accounts and 2025-26 BE — the money moved to the Union line, which is larger
claims.d: RBI Appendix II, J&K 'iii) Police' (revenue, MH 2055): ₹8,396.49 crore (2023-24 Accounts) → ₹6,437.13 crore (2024-25 BE) → ₹5,762.66 crore (2024-25 RE) → ₹2,248.49 crore (2025-26 BE). The Union took over the J&K Police budget from BE 2024-25 (FM budget speech 2024-07-23: about 11% of J&K's budget went to police; the Union to meet salary, pension and operational costs); it appears as item 6 of the Union's Demand 51 (Police, MHA): BE 2024-25 ₹9,789.42 crore (revenue ₹9,046.17 + capital ₹743.25), RE 2024-25 ₹8,665.94 crore (₹8,420.71 + ₹245.23), BE 2025-26 ₹9,325.73 crore (₹8,897.72 + ₹428.01); the 2024-25 Actual (₹8,553.38 crore) is recorded in the union-home file from the 2026-27 demand, not opened here. Overlap: in 2024-25 both the UT line (BE ₹6,437.13 / RE ₹5,762.66 crore) and the Union line carry police spending; in BE 2025-26 the two together are ₹11,574 crore (₹11,146 crore revenue-only) against ₹8,396 crore in 2023-24. The Union line includes capital and, per the reporting, pension, while the RBI row is revenue MH 2055 only. Opposition reading (The Wire, 2024-08-01): NC's Hasnain Masoodi called it 'further encroachment upon powers of J&K government'; Congress's Jairam Ramesh asked whether it is 'a Trojan Horse' for permanent control of the police from New Delhi; CPI(M)'s M.Y. Tarigami said the Home Ministry had assumed 'full control over J&K Police by taking over its budget'. The MHA's stated position (via reporting) is that a separate JKP budget is aligned with the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019.

claims.d: The 20-state set is the file's own: IJR's 18 large/mid-sized states plus Assam and Himachal Pradesh. narratives.claim: UP encounters are state policy — the Uttar Pradesh government runs a deliberate programme of killing suspects in police 'encounters'.
narratives.strongestCase: The UP government and UP Police publish 'encounter' tallies as achievements: UP Police data of 2024-12-30 counted 217 criminals killed in encounters since March 2017 (7,799 injured) and the DGP on 2025-12-31 put the cumulative figure at 266 killed in eight and a half years with 48 killed in 2025, the highest single year (both reported: the state's own claim, via India TV and Deccan Herald/PTI; the year-wise series before 2024 was not opened here). NHRC registered 16 and 11 cases of 'death in police encounter' in UP in FY2020-21 and FY2021-22 (LS UQ 1459, Annexure II) — the largest count of any state outside Chhattisgarh and J&K — and 8, 10, 12, 11 and 15 cases of death in UP police custody in FY2021-22 → FY2025-26. UP has the largest force (actual 134 per lakh × 23.4 crore people ≈ 313,686, a derived figure: BPR&D Jan 2024 per-lakh ratio × NCRB 2022 projected population) and the largest absolute vacancy.
narratives.strongestCounter: Per population the NHRC encounter-death series does not single UP out: FY2020-21/FY2021-22 cases were UP 16/11 against Gujarat 0/0, Maharashtra 1/1, Punjab 1/2, Assam 4/18, Chhattisgarh 24/30 and J&K 5/45 (LS UQ 1459); per crore population UP (≈0.7 and ≈0.5) is close to Punjab (≈0.3/0.7) and below Assam (≈1.1/5.1), Chhattisgarh (≈8/10) and J&K. The state's on-record position is self-defence: in the PUCL petition the UP government told the Supreme Court (affidavit reported 2023-10-04) that there is 'regular monitoring of police self-defence action in which accused persons have died', with district-wise daily reports to DGP headquarters since 2018 and review of magisterial and NHRC enquiries; the SC had on 2023-08-11 asked for a comprehensive affidavit on 183 encounters since 2017. Separately, there is a documented discrepancy between the two official series: NCRB Crime in India 2024 Table 16B.4 has a column 'Accidentally in Police Operations/Encounters' and UP returned 0 in every column (23 of 28 states returned 0 in total), while UP Police's own published count for the same period was in the tens (217 to 2024-12-28 cumulative; 266 to 2025-12-31) — the state-supplied NCRB table and the state's press tally cannot both describe the same events (analytic; see claim c026). NCRB also returned 0 deaths in UP police custody for 2024 against NHRC's 11 cases registered in FY2024-25.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A year-wise UP government statement of persons killed in police action since 2017-03-20 (PIB or uppolice.gov.in), set beside the same figure for Maharashtra, Assam, Punjab, Chhattisgarh and Telangana per lakh police and per crore population; an MHA/NHRC answer extending the LS UQ 1459 encounter-death series to FY2022-23 onward (not located in this pass); the magisterial-enquiry outcomes under the Supreme Court's PUCL (2014) guidelines and the SC's disposal of the 2018 PUCL petition; and a reconciliation of NCRB Table 16B.4 with the state's own tally.

narratives.claim: Kerala has the best-funded police in India.
narratives.strongestCase: The narrative's documented origin is the Common Cause / Lokniti-CSDS Status of Policing in India Report 2019 (released 2019-08-27), whose Police Adequacy Index ranked Delhi first and Kerala second (then Maharashtra) on staffing, infrastructure and budget use across 22 states — not on funding level. Kerala ranks 4th overall in IJR 2025 (prisons 3rd, human-resources theme 1st) but 13th / 14th / 17th / 15th of 18 large and mid-sized states in the IJR police pillar (IJR 1–4: 2019 / 2021 / 2022 / 2025). Constable vacancy was 4.6% as of 01.01.2022 (IJR, 1st of 18) against 26% in UP and 44% in West Bengal; actual strength 153 per lakh is close to sanctioned (172). No source was found in which the 'best-funded' phrasing itself circulates; the money framing is the file's restatement of the staffing finding (see gaps).
narratives.strongestCounter: On money Kerala is mid-table: ₹1,212 per capita in 2023-24 Accounts, 13th of 20 states with population above 70 lakh (the file's own set: IJR's 18 large/mid-sized states plus Assam and Himachal Pradesh; 11th of IJR's 18), below 12 states — Punjab ₹2,615, Telangana ₹2,356, Himachal ₹2,036, Uttarakhand ₹1,960, Haryana ₹1,937, Chhattisgarh ₹1,727, Maharashtra ₹1,667, Jharkhand ₹1,573, Assam ₹1,478, Andhra Pradesh ₹1,346, Tamil Nadu ₹1,343 and Karnataka ₹1,258; its police share of revenue expenditure (3.03%) is below the all-states 4.67%; IJR's own 2020-21 spend-per-person puts Kerala at ₹936 against Punjab ₹2,055. Per police person (derived: 2023-24 revenue spend ÷ actual strength Jan 2024) Kerala spends about ₹7.9 lakh, roughly 17th of the 20, against Telangana ≈₹14.6 lakh and Punjab ≈₹11.2 lakh. Kerala's staffing lead is also narrower on total vacancy: on BPR&D Jan 2024 figures (PRS Table 22) Kerala's 11.0% is 3rd of 20 behind Tamil Nadu (7.0%) and Himachal (10.3%), and IJR officer vacancy (23.9%, Jan 2022) ranks 9th of 18.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A BPR&D expenditure-per-police-person table showing Kerala at the top, or evidence that Kerala's capital outlay (MH 4055, not in RBI's revenue row) is unusually large: Kerala would need about ₹165 crore more (≈₹46 per person) to pass Karnataka on per-capita spend, and Karnataka's capital outlay is excluded too.

narratives.claim: Police vacancies are the real problem — fill the sanctioned posts and policing outcomes will follow.
narratives.strongestCase: All-India actual strength is 155 against 197 sanctioned per lakh (21% vacancy, Jan 2024; 24% in Jan 2016); Bihar runs at 80 per lakh with 40% vacancy and West Bengal at 106 with 36%; officer vacancies above 40% in Bihar, Rajasthan, UP and Tripura (IJR Jan 2022) mean investigations are supervised thinly.
narratives.strongestCounter: Custodial-death rates (the only outcome series in this file) do not track vacancy. Over FY2021-22 → FY2025-26 (to 15.03.2026) NHRC-registered police-custody death cases per lakh actual police (Jan 2024; derived) run Gujarat (23% vacancy) ≈91 and Maharashtra (13%) ≈49, against Bihar (40%) ≈76, West Bengal (36%) ≈40 and Tamil Nadu (7%) ≈22; across the 18 IJR large states the correlation between vacancy share and that rate is weak (r ≈ 0.2 on the file's computation; the cross-examiner's run gave ≈0.14). Bihar reported 1 and West Bengal 0 deaths in police custody to NCRB for 2024 (Tables 16A.1 + 16A.2) against NHRC registrations of 10 and 7 in FY2024-25 (Bihar 19 in FY2025-26, the highest of any state that year, Rajasthan 18). Gujarat and Maharashtra have the highest counts in NCRB 2024 (17, 16) and in the NHRC five-year sums (85, 101), but not in NHRC FY2025-26. Sanctioned strength is itself an administrative number: UP's sanctioned ratio fell slightly from 183.19 to 181 per lakh between Jan 2020 (RS UQ 3266) and Jan 2024 (PRS Table 22) while actual was flat at 133.85 → 134, and 'vacancy' is partly posts never meant to be filled. The 21% (all-India), 40% (Bihar) and 36% (West Bengal) vacancy shares are derived as 1 − actual/sanctioned from PRS's per-lakh ratios (PRS prints the ratios, not percentages), and PRS Table 22 carries an unexplained asterisk on Bihar.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A panel of states over 2016–2024 relating vacancy share to charge-sheeting rates, conviction rates and custodial-death rates with population and GSDP controls; DoPO absolute strengths are needed first.

symmetryCheck: Same lens on both sides (party as text from the fetched CM lists; party in FY2024-25, spend 2023-24 Accounts, strength 01.01.2024, NHRC police-custody death cases FY2024-25). BJP-run (UP, GJ, MP, RJ, CT, HR, UT, AS, AR, GA, TR): median police revenue spend per capita 2023-24 ₹1,727, median actual police per lakh 174, median vacancy share 20.7%, median NHRC cases per lakh actual police 6.3 (the ₹1,727 and 20.7% are Chhattisgarh's values from a year under the outgoing INC government). Opposition-run (KA, KL, TN, WB, TG, PB, HP, JH): ₹1,458, 156.5 per lakh, 15.5% vacancy, 7.56 cases per lakh police. Restricted to large states (population ≥ 3 crore: BJP-run UP, GJ, MP, RJ, AS; opposition-run KA, KL, TN, WB, TG, PB, JH) the groups overlap on every measure: per capita ₹912–₹1,478 vs ₹1,012–₹2,615; NHRC cases per lakh police 3.51–21.93 vs 1.64–11.77. The highest custodial-death counts in NCRB 2024 and in the NHRC five-year sums are a BJP-run state (Gujarat) and a coalition state (Maharashtra), level on NHRC FY2024-25 (14 each); the thinnest force and the highest FY2025-26 NHRC count are in JD(U)-led Bihar; the states returning 0 cases against their own police personnel in NCRB 2024 Table 16A.5 are Bihar, Manipur, Meghalaya and Sikkim (UP returns 88, West Bengal 16), while the states returning 0 deaths in police custody against NHRC registrations > 0 are AP, JH, ML, OD, UP, UK and WB — across parties. What the lens shows is that the outcome series are dominated by reporting practice and small numbers, not by party; the file prints it either way.

State police demands with pay/capital split for Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka: state budget portals 000; where: each state finance department's 'Demands for Grants' volume for the Home department (Maharashtra Demand B-?, Karnataka DDG Vol. 2, TN Demand 22 Police, WB Demand 23 Home, Bihar Demand 22).

UP Grant 26 pay component: the '01-वेतन' (salary) object head is printed per sub-head across 44 lines with multi-line wrapping; a reliable sum was not extracted (district police main salary line ≈ ₹10,935–11,856 crore across the four columns, column mapping uncertain) — record as gap rather than a pay row.
RBI State Finances back-issues 2011-12 → 2023-24 (Appendix II by state): not fetched; where: rbi.org.in AnnualPublications year selector (postback) → PublicationsView ids per edition.
NCRB Crime in India 2022 and 2023 Volume III URLs (chapter 16A/16B state tables): not located; where: ncrb.gov.in/en/crime-india year pages (client-rendered) or data.opencity.in mirrors.

UP Police's own year-wise count of persons killed in police 'encounters' since 2017: only cumulative press figures were opened (217 to 2024-12-28 via India TV; 266 to 2025-12-31 and 48 in 2025 via Deccan Herald/PTI); the year-by-year series 2017–2023 and any PIB/uppolice.gov.in statement were not fetched; where: UP Police press notes, UP government statements on PIB and uppolice.gov.in.

Ruling party for Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Jharkhand before their latest CM (2022 and 2023 base years): only the current CM list was fetched; where: Wikipedia lists of chief ministers of those states, or ECI results.

Commissionerates outside UP and Maharashtra (Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Surat, Jaipur, Indore, Patna, Kochi, Kozhikode, Coimbatore and ~40 others in DoPO's table): not written as entities because no primary listing was opened; where: DoPO table of commissionerates, or each state police website.
Deaths in police firing (as distinct from custodial deaths) by state for 2022–2023: NCRB 16B tables opened only for 2024.

NHRC 'death in police encounter' cases by state after FY2021-22: LS UQ 1459 (26.07.2022) covers FY2020-21 and FY2021-22 only; a later MHA answer extending the series was not located; where: sansad.in Q&A search on 'encounter death' / NHRC annual reports.

The narrative 'Kerala has the best-funded police in India' was not found circulating in that wording; its documented root is SPIR 2019's Police Adequacy Index (Delhi, then Kerala, then Maharashtra on staffing, infrastructure and budget use). The money framing is this file's restatement, written so it can be tested.

J&K Police 2024-25 Actual on the Union line (₹8,553.38 crore) is carried in the union-home file from the 2026-27 Demand 51 document, which returned 404 from this sandbox; the residual ₹2,248 crore in J&K's own 2025-26 BE police line is unexplained.
